Plan: Cigna (Commercial/ACA), State of Louisiana
CPT Code: 27130 (Arthroplasty, acetabular and proximal femoral prosthetic replacement; total hip replacement)
Surgical Provider: Dr. Okafor, MD
Reference Number: POC-892F80BC2E-98290
Date of Denial Notice: August 21, 2026

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to formally appeal Cigna’s denial of prior authorization for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), to be performed by Dr. Okafor, MD. The denial letter dated August 21, 2026, states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. 

Upon review of my clinical records and Cigna’s governing medical policy, "CIGNA MEDICAL COVERAGE POLICIES - MUSCULOSKELETAL CMM-313: Hip Replacement/ Arthroplasty" (Effective Date: August 04, 2026), my clinical presentation clearly meets all of Cigna’s established criteria for the medical necessity of a total hip replacement. 

Below, I map my clinical documentation directly to the specific requirements outlined in Policy CMM-313:

1. Case-by-Case Determination of Medical Necessity
Cigna’s policy states that "The determination of medical necessity for the performance of hip resurfacing and hip replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis." My specific case presents a severe, progressive pathology that has failed to improve under conservative care, making surgical intervention the only viable path to restore my basic mobility.

2. Imaging Criteria Met
Cigna's policy states that total hip replacement is considered medically necessary when there is:
"Imaging shows ANY of the following findings: 
◦ Tönnis Grade 2-3 osteoarthritis"

My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph performed on June 29, 2026, reveals that my joint space is narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, accompanied by subchondral sclerosis and osteophyte formation. This advanced joint space narrowing and structural damage clinically correlates to Tönnis Grade 2-3 osteoarthritis, fully satisfying the imaging requirement of the policy.

3. Symptom and Functional Criteria Met
Cigna's policy requires that "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:" (Note: The exact literal sub-text defining these symptoms was not retrieved from the 2026 policy document; therefore, these criteria are addressed in plain clinical terms without quotes). My clinical documentation establishes both severe, function-limiting pain at short distances and a profound loss of hip function interfering with my activities of daily living:
* Function-Limiting Pain: I have suffered from 12 months of progressive, severe hip pain that is unrelieved by rest. I am now forced to ambulate with a cane, and my walking tolerance is strictly limited to only one city block.
* Loss of Hip Function: Due to my severe range-of-motion limitations caused by pain, I cannot carry out standard activities of daily living, such as being unable to put on my shoes unassisted. Dr. Okafor's physical exam confirmed highly restricted range of motion limited by pain and positive provocative testing on my affected side.

4. Failure of Non-Surgical Management Met
Cigna's policy requires:
"Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration"

My clinical record documents an exhaustive, multi-modal conservative treatment regimen that far exceeds the required 3-month duration, without providing lasting relief:
* Supervised Physical Therapy: I completed a 10-week course of supervised physical therapy focusing on hip abductor strengthening and gait training. This treatment spanned from April 22, 2026, to July 1, 2026, totaling 24 completed visits, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
* Oral Medications: I have taken prescription NSAIDs daily for 6 months with inadequate pain relief.
* Intra-articular Injections: I received a therapeutic corticosteroid injection on May 13, 2026, which yielded only 3 weeks of temporary, partial relief before my severe symptoms recurred.

My conservative care timeline spans from April 2026 through August 2026, demonstrating over 4 months of active, documented failure of provider-directed non-surgical management.

5. Clinical Safety and Optimization
I am highly optimized for an excellent surgical outcome. I have a BMI of 29 (which does not trigger the extended 6-month conservative trial required for patients with a BMI over 40). Furthermore, I have no active local or systemic infection, do not smoke, and have no untreated substance use issues.

Conclusion:
Because I meet or exceed every requirement set forth in Cigna Policy CMM-313, I request that you overturn this denial and immediately authorize my total hip replacement (CPT 27130) so that Dr. Okafor can proceed with my surgery. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I have attached the supporting clinical documents for your review.

Sincerely,

Morgan Ellison
[Signature]

Attachments:
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph report dated June 29, 2026
- Supervised physical therapy discharge note (April 22, 2026 to July 1, 2026, 24 visits)
- Dr. Okafor's clinical evaluation and exam notes (documenting NSAID use, injection on May 13, 2026, and ADL limitations)
